newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end up on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end up on shortcovering.

text.p: CME lumber futures remained supported at higher levels at Tuesday's close from shortcovering and speculative buying prompted by an oversold condition following recent limit declines, traders said.
Lumber closed $7.60 per tbf higher to $1.00 lower with July pacing the gain at $354.70 and September up $4.60 at $348.60 per tbf.

Despite two days of limit losses that resulted in an expanded trading limit of $15, futures rose from the start on short covering prompted by an oversold market. Futures got way ahead of falling cash prices, traders said.

Futures were showing a cash equivalent of near $335 at Monday's close while spruce was reportedly in the $345 to $350 per tbf area for mill asking prices and the last Random Lengths official quote was $358 per tbf.
Traders also noted that spreads were turning bullish from a recent bearish stance which may indicate an up move in the futures market.
Buying interest was mixed with Cargill Investor Services a scale-up seller, pit sources said.
